full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: - This appeal is by the pre-emptor, by leave, is against the judgment of Februarys 22, 1995 of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 630 of 1981 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and order dated May 30, 1979 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge), Sylhet, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1977 allowing the same and thereupon setting aside the judgment and order dated February 28, 1977 of the 1st Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Sylhet in Miscellaneous Case (pre-emption) No. 76 of 1970 allowing the same. The Miscellaneous case was filed by the petitioner under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 in respect of the sale which took place on 5.11.1969 clamming him to be a co-sharer of the land so transferred alleging that the purchaser is a stranger. It was also the contention that no notice of the sale was served upon the pre-emptor. It was the pre-emptor's claim that the land so transferred to the pre-emptee is homestead with adjuncts not connected with agriculture. 

 2. The prayer for pre-emption was contested primarily on the ground that the Miscellaneous case filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act was not maintainable since the land is not non-agricultural land and as such pre-emptor was required to file application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (SAT Act). It was also contended that the transfer sought to be pre-empted took place by 2 deeds and that as the pre-emptor has not filed 2 separate cases for that two transactions, the prayer for pre-emption so sought in a single case is not maintainable. 

 3. The trial Court framed issues as to maintainability of the Miscellaneous case under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act as well as whether pre-emptor is entitled to pre-empt the land transferred on 5.11.1969. It may be mentioned that there was prayer for pre-emption by the some of the opposite parties who got them transposed as co-petitioners in the Miscellaneous case. 

 4. The trial Court allowed the prayer for pre-emption upon rejecting the prayer of the co-petitioners. The pre-emptee as well as the co-petitioners filed appeals being Nos. 81 of 1977 and 68 of 1977 respectively. The appellate Court on consideration .of the evidence on record arrived at the finding that the land sought to be pre-emted is not within the Municipal area and as such the pre-emptor was required to file petition seeking pre-emption under section 96 of the SAT Act and thereupon held that the Miscellaneous case so filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is not maintainable. The appellate Court also held that the co-petitioners are not co-sharers of the land sought to be pre-empted. On the aforesaid findings allowed the appeal filed by the pre-emptee i.e. Appeal No. 81 of 1977 and dismissed the appeal of the co-petitioners i.e. Appeal No. 68 of 1977. The appellate Court upon allowing the appeal of the pre-emptee dismissed the Miscellaneous case and set aside the judgment and order of the trial Court. The pre-emptor alone as against the judgment of the appellate Court moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on the finding that the land including the homestead land situates in the rural area. The High Court Division considering the nature and character of the suit holding and its situation held that the homestead with adjunct is very much connected with agriculture and that there is nothing on record to show that the suit holding was used for the purpose not connected with agriculture and it is non-agricultural land for all practical purpose and the suit holding being homestead situated in the rural area is an agricultural land and pre-emption as regard such kind of land could only be sought under section 96 of the SAT Act. 

 5. Leave was granted to consider the contention of the pre-emptor that the case land being part of the homestead of the petitioner (pre-emptor), a Mason, having no cultivation and the case land as not used for the purpose connected with the agriculture or horticulture the High Court Division was in error in law in holding that the pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act is not maintainable. 

 6. The Miscellaneous Case seeking pre-emption in respect of the transfer that took place on 5.11.1969 was filed under section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act. The undisputed position is that the land sought to be pre-empted is in rural area. No evidence was brought on record from the side of the pre-emptor that the tenancy was for non-agricultural purpose. No material was also brought on record that the settlement was given for non-agricultural purpose. It is also not disputed that that the land sought to be pre-empted is outside the Municipal area. The contention that the pre-emptor is a Mason and the pre-emptee is a service holder and not directly engaged in cultivation and as such the homestead of the parties is non-agricultural land appears to be legally not well-conceived one and also not legally sustainable since it is the purpose for which settlement was obtained or the settlement was given that would be the determining fact whether the land is non-agricultural or agricultural. 

 7. In the instant case nothing has been brought on record that the tenancy was created for non-agricultural purpose. The character of the land is always referable to the purpose for which settlement was made. If the settlement was made for a purpose unconnected with the agriculture in that case the land even if used for the purpose connected with the agriculture would remain as non-agricultural land. It may also be mentioned that the purpose of the land may also be referable to its location or situation i.e. if it is within the urban area or in other words within the Municipal area in that case the land would assume the character of non-agricultural land even if the said land was for the purpose connected with agriculture. Since the land within the Municipality or in the urban area is ultimately will be used for residential purpose in such situation an application seeking pre-emption in respect of the said land under section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act would be very much maintainable. We are of the view that the character of the land which are within the urban area or municipal area is determined keeping in view the purpose for which such land is likely to be used. The homestead and the adjuncts thereto of an agricultural raiyat in the rural area can hardly be considered non-agricultural land in the absence of establishing that the said land was taken settlement for non-agricultural purpose. 

 8. The homestead of an agricultural raiyat is included within the agricultural holding. From the evidence on record it is seen that the land is in the rural area and that the homestead with adjuncts are being used in connection with agriculture purpose and as such we are of the view the land sought to be pre-empted is agricultural land. From the pre-emptor's side as stated herein-before no material was brought on record to show that the land was taken settlement for non-agricultural purpose. It is the uniform view that character/ nature of particular land is to be determined keeping in view the purpose for which tenancy was created or that settlement was made or that purpose for which lease was taken. It is also the uniform view that the land within the municipal area is pre-emptable under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. 

 9. Since the land sought to be pre-empted is admittedly in the rural area and that it having not been established that the settlement of the land sought to be pre-empted was taken for the purpose other then agricultural purpose we are of the view that the High Court Division was not in error in discharging the Rule which was obtained against the judgment of the appellate Court dismissing the Miscellaneous case filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act upon arriving at the finding that the land sought to be pre-empted is agricultural land.
